title_original: Warwick Thornton, Teona Strugar Mitevska & Myroslav Slaboshpytskiy Set For Rotterdam’s Cinemart

blocks.text: The International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR) Pro has unveiled the 20 projects selected for the 44th edition of its co-financing platform CineMart as well as work-in-progress showcase Darkroom and the Safe Harbour stand, for filmmakers who have experienced forced migration.
All three strands fall under the umbrella of IFFR’s Co-Production market running from January 31 to February 3, 2027.

The Cinemart selection includes upcoming films by Warwick Thornton ( The New Boy), Teona Strugar Mitevska ( Mother ), Myroslav Slaboshpytskiy ( The Tribe ), Damien Hauser ( Memory of Princess Mumbi ) and Guido Hendrikx ( Stranger in Paris). Scroll down for full list of projects and credits.

blocks.text: Dedicated to projects by filmmakers who have presented work in the Tiger Competition or Bright Future in the last 10 years, Darkroom will showcase ten projects looking for completion funding, sales agents and festival selections. The projects are also in the running for IFFR Pro Awards.
Watch on Deadline

They include working titled Tahmina by Aboozar Amini, who previously made waves with Kabul, City in the Wind , and Elisa’s Miller Legítima about a rape victim charged with murder after she kills one of the attackers in self-defence. Nicolás Celis who took credits on Emilia Pérez is producing

“From contemporary reinventions of the Western and working-class musical fables to personal and urgent stories of displacement and identity, this year’s CineMart, Darkroom and Safe Harbour selections unites an extraordinary range of cinematic voices – filmmakers reclaiming histories, subverting familiar genres and finding fresh ways to tell stories about our world,” said Marten Rabarts, Head of IFFR Pro.

“That we can bring together celebrated auteurs and festival alumni working in independent cinema with filmmakers embarking on their first features is something quintessentially Rotterdam. It is the strength, relevance and originality of the cinematic vision, rather than the stage of a filmmaker’s career, that draws us to a project,” he added.

A number of films presented at CineMart or Darkroom are also confirmed for the upcoming edition of the festival. Four Seasons In Java by Kamila Andini and Elephants in the Fog by Abinash Bikram Shah will play in the Limelight section. Kaktarua by Yudhajit Basu and Prithvijoy Ganguly will world premiere in the Bright Future lineup. El Mundo es Nuestro by Francisco Márquez and The Station by Sara Ishaq will screen in the Harbour sidebar.

Baile Director: Nelly Shylova (Ukraine – Ireland based) A Ukrainian filmmaker joins fellow refugees in learning Irish in a country where relatively few locals speak it. Together, they explore the language and the unexpected reasons that draw newcomers towards it.

Flotilla Director: Mohammed Almughanni (Palestine – Italy based) A captain of a humanitarian flotilla attempting to break the siege of Gaza must hold together a deeply divided crew whose conflicting ideologies, beliefs, and personal convictions threaten to jeopardize the mission.

Interrupted Director & Producer: Raha Faridi (Iran – Germany based) At a kiosk in Germany, Reza, a blind Iranian cinephile, transforms customers’ memories into imagined films. When Raha, an Iranian filmmaker, begins recording their conversations, documentary reality slips into live action, animation and comic-like fantasy, only to be interrupted by the shop bell. Through their cross-generational dialogue, Reza’s own hidden past gradually emerges.

Ping, Pong Director: Saleh Saadi (Palestine) Producer: May Jabareen (Philistine Films, Palestine/Jordan) As war erupts in Gaza, a few kilometres away in a village between Nazareth and Haifa, Issam returns to his childhood home to stay with his parents, for the first time since his brother’s passing a year prior. He finds unexpected solace in nightly ping-pong games hosted by his neighbor, forging a friendship that helps him confront his sorrow and rediscover resilience amidst the chaos.
